SUMMARY: The PR correctly handles bounded wildcards but crashes on unbounded wildcards.
POINTS:
- [auto-value-moshi/src/main/java/com/ryanharter/auto/value/moshi/AutoValueMoshiExtension.java:497-506] Unbounded wildcards like `?` throw `IllegalArgumentException` at compile time instead of generating valid code — fix: handle empty bounds by defaulting to `Types.subtypeOf(Object.class)`.

suspicions.observation: The wildcard handling checks `wildcard.lowerBounds.size() == 1` and `wildcard.upperBounds.size() == 1`, but throws `IllegalArgumentException` when both are empty (size == 0). An unbounded wildcard `?` (e.g., `List<?>`) has zero lower bounds and zero upper bounds in JavaPoet's WildcardTypeName.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Using an unbounded wildcard like `?` (e.g., `List<?>`) will throw `IllegalArgumentException` at compile time instead of generating valid code like `Types.subtypeOf(Object.class)`.

bugs.observation: The wildcard handling checks `wildcard.lowerBounds.size() == 1` and `wildcard.upperBounds.size() == 1`, but throws `IllegalArgumentException` when both are empty (size == 0). An unbounded wildcard `?` (e.g., `List<?>`) has zero lower bounds and zero upper bounds in JavaPoet's WildcardTypeName.
bugs.suspected_bug: Using an unbounded wildcard like `?` (e.g., `List<?>`) will throw `IllegalArgumentException` at compile time instead of generating valid code like `Types.subtypeOf(Object.class)`.
bugs.evidence: AutoValueMoshiExtension.java:504-506 - when both wildcard.lowerBounds.size()==0 AND wildcard.upperBounds.size()==0 (unbounded wildcard ?), the else branch throws IllegalArgumentException instead of generating Types.subtypeOf(Object.class). The test with List<?> fails because MoshiJsonAdapter is never generated due to the exception.
bugs.reproduction:
./gradlew :auto-value-moshi:test --tests "com.ryanharter.auto.value.moshi.AutoValueMoshiExtensionTest.unboundedWildcard"
exit=1

test/Test.java:8: error: cannot find symbol
    return new AutoValue_Test.MoshiJsonAdapter(moshi);
                             ^
  symbol:   class MoshiJsonAdapter

        + "\n"
        + "  public static final class MoshiJsonAdapter extends JsonAdapter<Foo> {\n"
        + "    private static final String[] NAMES = new String[] {\"a\", \"b\"};\n"
        + "    private static final JsonReader.Options OPTIONS = JsonReader.Options.of(NAMES);\n"
        + "    private final JsonAdapter<String> aAdapter;\n"
        + "    private final JsonAdapter<String> bAdapter;\n"
        + "    public AutoValue_FooJsonAdapter(Moshi moshi) {\n"
        + "      this.aAdapter = moshi.adapter(String.class);\n"
        + "      this.bAdapter = adapter(moshi, \"b\");\n"
        + "    }\n"
        + "    @Override\n"
        + "    public Foo fromJson(JsonReader reader) throws IOException {\n"
        + "      reader.beginObject();\n"

        + "          }\n"
        + "          case 1: {\n"

        + "            break;\n"

        + "      return new AutoValue_Foo(a, b);\n"

        + "      writer.beginObject();\n"
        + "      writer.name(\"a\");\n"
        + "      aAdapter.toJson(writer, value.a());\n"
        + "      writer.name(\"b\");\n"
        + "      bAdapter.toJson(writer, value.b());\n"
        + "      writer.endObject();\n"
        + "    }\n"
        + "    private JsonAdapter adapter(Moshi moshi, String methodName) {\n"
        + "      try {\n"

        + "    }\n"

    assertAbout(javaSources())
        .that(Arrays.asList(annotation, adapter, source))
